title: Lagrange multipliers
goal: Find the best value of $f(x, y)$ when you are forced to stay on a fixed constraint path $g(x, y) = k$ (like a fixed budget) using Lagrange multipliers: $f_x = \lambda g_x$, $f_y = \lambda g_y$, and $g(x, y) = k$.

beforeThis.skill: Cleanest algebra strategy: solve $f_x = \lambda g_x$ and $f_y = \lambda g_y$ for $\lambda$, set them equal to get a simple relationship between $x$ and $y$, and plug that into the constraint $g(x, y) = k$.

links.label: Precalculus: Power functions and solving nonlinear systems

seeIt.title: Understanding Lagrange Multipliers Visually
seeIt.creator: Serpentine Integral
seeIt.watchFor: Shows visually why the highest and lowest values of $f(x, y)$ along a constraint curve $g(x, y) = k$ occur where their level curves are tangent ($\nabla f = \lambda \nabla g$).

questions.asking: Explain geometrically or algebraically whether $x^2 + y^2$ has a minimum or maximum on the hyperbola $xy = 1$, and find all points on $xy = 1$ where that extremum occurs.
questions.statement:
1. Does the function $f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2$ have a maximum or a minimum on the curve $xy = 1$? Explain.
  2. Find all maxima and minima of $f(x, y)$ on the curve $xy = 1$.

questions.asking: Find the minimum value of $z = x^2 + y^2$ on the curve $x^2 y = 1$ and state the coordinates $(x, y)$ where it occurs.
questions.statement: Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the minimum value of $z = x^2 + y^2$ subject to $x^2 y = 1$. At which point or points does the minimum occur?

questions.asking: Set up Lagrange multipliers ($f_x = \lambda g_x$, $f_y = \lambda g_y$, and $x^2 + 2y^2 = 1$), eliminate $\lambda$ to relate $x$ and $y$, and compare the values of $xy$ at the resulting points.
questions.statement:
Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum and minimum values of

$$f(x, y) = xy$$

subject to the constraint

$$x^2 + 2y^2 = 1.$$

questions.asking: Find the maximum and minimum values of $U = 9x^{1/3}y^{2/3}$ along the budget segment $3200x + 200y = 80{,}000$ with $x \ge 0$ and $y \ge 0$.
questions.statement: Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum and minimum values of the utility function $U = f(x, y) = 9x^{1/3}y^{2/3}$, subject to the constraint $g(x, y) = 3200x + 200y = 80{,}000$, where $x \ge 0$ and $y \ge 0$.
